utterances.text: Well, the Mijat Tomic Battalion was part of the Herceg Stjepan Brigade, it was its third battalion, and it was made up of men who were exclusively soldiers from the Jablanica municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: May I interrupt you, sir. I would like to ask the witness if in connection with the order which we are now just looking at, that is the -- which is 2037, and in the -- in paragraph 1, it says that: "I hereby order to cease immediately offensive activities against the Bosnian army and artillery fire on Jablanica." That was signed by Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic. I would like to ask you, sir, if the artillery fire has indeed stopped after the -- this order was issued, that is in April, the -- I would say April 22nd.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, not. Events were to show that the fiercest attack against Jablanica was to take place on the 24th of April, or did take place on the 24th of April, when Tuta's deputy Cikota was killed. And then you have in the documents that in retaliation for the death of that man four soldiers belonging to the HVO army were killed who were in Sovici and still captured up there. But the major attack took place against Jablanica on the 24th of April, precisely two days after this order had been issued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And then going forward some days later, did you come to know that a group of persons actually went and toured, if you can call it that, went to Sovici, a group involving again Mr. Petkovic, Mr. Halilovic, and others?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who from Jablanica, from in the Jablanica ABiH, who was involved in these meetings, if anyone, or the tour at the Sovici area?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not quite sure whether any of the representatives of the army from Jablanica were there. Maybe, but I'm not quite sure just now. I know that Halilovic went.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Kovacevic went?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say for certain. I don't want to say something I'm not sure of. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. Can I ask you, please, to look at document 568. Do you have that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: He has it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, from your familiarity with the Jablanica area and what you came to know, can you tell us what this location is?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the house belonging to the late Jure Juric from Doljani. He lived in Croatia, in Rovinj, and this is where the headquarters of the Mijat Tomic Battalion was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is this close -- is this considered to be in the village or area of Doljani?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Doljani is a very widespread village, houses scattered around. This house is near the church in Doljani. You can't see it on this photograph, but the church isn't far from there. And then there's the hamlet of Orlovac a little further down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I next ask you to look at document 2182.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: He's getting there.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that around this time, the date of this order, which is the 4th of May, 1993, that Muslim civilians from the Sovici area were, to your knowledge, released or transported out of the area?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civilians from Sovici, contrary to certain previous orders from Mr. Petkovic, because in a previous order I think he ordered that they be released towards Jablanica, but after this time, sometime later, they were taken towards Gornji Vakuf and then released there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. We'll come back to those events in a moment. Can I ask you also to look at Exhibit 2218. This is a document of the Herceg Stjepan Brigade dated the 7th of May, 1993, in Doljani. Can I ask you, please, to look at the fourth paragraph starting with the words: "The transfer of detainees ..." You said just a moment ago that in fact the persons released were sent towards Gornji Vakuf, and is that what it says in this paragraph, is that so indicated?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were driven off probably in buses towards Gornji Vakuf. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Further up in the second paragraph of that letter just in passing, did you have any knowledge of what happened to the members -- the male members, the men, of the ABiH units in Sovici-Doljani? What happened to them after this conflict on the 16th and 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We later learnt that they were taken to the camp in Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you learn, sir, around this time that Muslim property was confiscated or stolen in mid-April -- the second half of April 1993 in the Sovici-Doljani area?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We learned about that from the people who arrived. Some of them had to make their way through the woods and forests, and they would trickle into Jablanica for days. And we learnt that everything had been looted up there, that all the houses and all the property there had been looted, and that the buildings had been set fire to, including two religious sites. If there was anything that was Muslim in the area, it no longer existed -- or anything that was Muslim in the area no longer existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you, please, to look at Exhibit 2372. If I can direct your attention to the section or paragraph with the marking Roman numeral I, and to your knowledge and based on the reports that you received from Muslims coming from these villages at the time, is that consistent with what was happening? Is what is said in paragraph Roman numeral I consistent with what was happening?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, in that first paragraph it says that everything that belonged to the Muslims shall be considered the spoils of war. Now, you had a military command. Could you enlighten the Chamber what was considered spoils of war? If you know, tell us; if not, you can tell us you don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, spoils of war, what -- when the units are in combat, what they seize from each other. That's the spoils of war. The spoils of war should not be considered to be what you seize from the population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that's your definition of the spoils of war, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there was no immovable property, it was set fire to. Now, all the movable property, well everybody knows what movable property refers to, and that was considered to be the spoils of war and it shall belong to the HZ HB Croatian Defence Council. That was how they defined it. That was how they proclaimed it. Now, it's another matter what international war law considers the spoils of war to be, their definition.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Sir, just before then we finish your testimony, and we're almost -- we've almost completed it, a couple of matters I'd just like to touch upon. There was later, after this time, there was a horrible atrocity that was committed in the Croat village of Grabovica. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that at the trial of Tuta and Stela. I personally as a human being consider that to be the greatest shame, very shameful for the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was an act which should never have happened. Civilians who were completely unprotected who didn't represent a danger to anybody were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell the Judges whether any ABiH forces or soldiers from -- to your knowledge were involved in that action at Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At Grabovica or -- because I was going to ask you about later, there was also a subsequent military action at Doljani, but let me ask -- I'm now focusing on Grabovica and whether units from Jablanica were involved in what happened at Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody from Jablanica took part down there. Grabovica belongs to the Mostar municipality; it wasn't our area of responsibility. And I think that this Tribunal, because there were trials here -- a trial -- the trial of Sefer Halilovic, I think that the Tribunal knows full well who the perpetrators were, parts of the units of the army from Sarajevo who had perpetrated those crimes. And I as a human being am very sorry. First of all, the courts in Bosnia-Herzegovina who were supposed to solve the problem didn't. They didn't have the will or the power to do so, whichever, I don't know. And then Sefer Halilovic was taken to trial and he was released, and I don't think that justice was served in that instance and that those who perpetrated the crimes in Grabovica should be held responsible and accountable.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In the town of Jablanica, there was a facility called the museum. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What kind of a museum was this?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was a museum from -- of the fourth offensive from World War II. It was a large building built in the 1970s. Joint forces and money from the whole of Yugoslavia financed its building. It was a large facility, a large building. It had exhibition halls for weapons, military equipment, and other materiel. And it had a large cinema hall with 500 seats and a smaller hall. It had depots where the exhibits were housed. It had a lot of offices, halls, exhibition areas, a library. It was a very large facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: The witness said that it was a building to commemorate the -- I believe the fourth offensive from World War II. I wonder if it was a offensive by the partisan forces or by the German forces or by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Germans, World War II. I mean the Germans and the partisans. It was a large-scale offensive, and to commemorate that the museum was completed in 1978.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To pay homage to the partisans fighting against the Germans. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because there was a bit of an ambiguity there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, because it was -- the museum was a large facility, did it become a location where refugees were housed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when there was no more room to put them up in more suitable locations. In Jablanica, in fact, when these people arrived, our refugees, refugees from Jablanica, if I can put it that way, from Slatina and Doljani, the number of refugees surpassed 10.000. So a town numbering just 3.000 inhabitants suddenly had 10.000 refugees coming in, and three camps were built by the Council for Refugees and all the schools, nursery schools, gymnastics halls and all the larger facilities able to take in people were full. And there was no more space to accommodate anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that both Muslim and Croat refugees were housed at the museum?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you -- can you tell the Judges whether the conditions in the museum, the living conditions were the same for both the Muslim and Croat refugees?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were the same, but they were difficult conditions generally and life in Jablanica was very difficult, both for the domicile population and the refugees. Some of them were put up in camps, some in some joint facilities such as schools and the like, and the rest were -- the rest mostly spent the year in the basements and cellars of their houses because there was shelling on a daily basis and people were killed in the streets just as they were up at the front. So that life in town was very difficult for everybody, and for the people in the museum, the Muslims and Croats, it was especially difficult. There were a total of 200 Croats and 400 Muslims from Capljina and Stolac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, might I ask you: During this time-period, where was your family living?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My family also lived in the basement, just like all the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The people who -- the refugees at the museum, were both the Muslims and Croats able to move about the town of Jablanica, such as it was?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, everybody was able to move around of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, in addition to the refugees that were at the museum, were there also a number of prisoners of war, military persons who were also kept at the museum?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were. They were under the authority of the military police, and the 6th Corps was there at the time, because in the meantime the 4th Corps was separated because it was just active in Mostar. And so in the area of the municipalities of Jablanica and Konjic, part of Prozor and up towards Fojnica, the 6th ABiH army Corps was established. So if there were, and I do believe there were, prisoners of war, then they came under the authority of the military police battalion of the 6th Corps which was located there in the museum at Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges, if you recall, approximately how many of these prisoners of war were there, as distinct from the refugees.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't give you an exact figure. I think there were about 20, perhaps a little more.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Idrizovic, I thank you for your testimony and for coming to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And that completes our questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I think that counsel Karnavas is going to start off. We have two ways of going about this, either take the break straight away or take the break afterwards. Whatever suits you best. Which is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps we could take the break now; that way I can organise myself to be more efficient, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll reconvene at 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, you have 45 minutes and perhaps more if your colleagues have given you some of their time. But I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. I believe I have 15 extra minutes, so that would be approximately one hour. I'll try to be as efficient as I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to pick up where your left, just to finish up a point, and then I'll go into what I had planned to do. You were asked a question about prisoners, and you were asked a question about the museum, and at one point you said you thought, you thought, that there were prisoners in the museum, and then you were asked to give an approximation. Were you aware, sir, that we are in possession of a document from the Prosecution wherein it is alleged that you were involved or that prisoners were brought to you as commander of the Muslim army of the ABiH staff in Jablanica. Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only four individuals can be concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And those individuals were taken to a prison that was located in the basement of the municipal -- old building in Jablanica, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I provide you an explanation, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir, you're answering my questions. So -- one step at a time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I provide you with a broad explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First I want to know whether those people were taken in the basement of the municipal building in Jablanica, yes, no, I don't know, which of the three?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say yes, no, or I don't know. I can just describe what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, at that point in time you were the commander of the -- of the Muslim army of ABiH staff in Jablanica, were you not? And we're talking about, just to be -- to refresh your memory on or about 15th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what you're asking me about very well, and I know what I was, and I have already said that I was in charge of the men who provided security for facilities. On that day, on the 15th of April, when the town was shelled, then those responsible for the defence of the town met. There was the brigade commander, myself --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, I don't want an explanation. I'm sorry. I don't have enough time, sir, and I don't want explanations.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have a document here from the Prosecution that says that you were responsible for those people and those people were beaten under your responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, just a minute. As a witness, sir, you have certain rights and I'll read out certain rights that you have pursuant to the Rules. It's 90 of the Rules, paragraph (I). It says: "A witness may refuse to testify if he risks incriminating himself; however, the Chamber may compel the witness to testify, to answer the question. But no testimony can then be used as evidence against the witness unless it is for perjury." This means if the Prosecution puts questions to you about some sort of a violation, you can say that you don't want to answer the question; but if the Defence really wants you to answer the question, if it insists, and the Chamber wants you to answer the question, if in that case you answer the question you have a form of immunity. This is provided by the Rules. That means that the OTP cannot use the answer you give against you unless you are guilty of perjury. So now you understand how things work.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do, and I've been trying to provide an answer, but I was interrupted by counsel. Allow me to answer this question. He put a question to me, and I'd like to answer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The question was -- sir, sir, I only have so much time. I only have so much time. Let me read what I have, and I'm referring to document P 01884. I'll read slowly. Please follow along, sir. In the first paragraph towards the bottom part, it says: "Witnesses -- the witness has known all the soldiers because they lived in Jablanica. They were taken to see Safet Idrizovic, commander of the Muslim army ABiH staff in Jablanica. After brief questioning, he ordered the police to take him to prison, where they found KZ, a Croat from Jablanica. The prison was in the basement of the municipal building in Jablanica. They stayed there for about ten days. Muslim soldiers would come in occasionally and beat them or force them to beat each other." Sir, were you aware that this document was in the possession of the Prosecution? Did they show this to you during your proofing session? Because that's where I got it from.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with this document from the Tuta and Stela case. And I would still like to give you an answer, if you allow me to do so. If not, I don't see the purpose of this exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you -- did you send those -- that prisoner to the basement of the municipal building of Jablanica, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you're denying what is in this document, under oath?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let him answer the question. Since he's being put a question, he has the right to say what he wants to say. What have you got to say about this? Apparently there's a document that says that certain individuals were placed in detention, you were in command, some of them were maltreated. What can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, let me describe what happened precisely. On the 15th of April when everything broke out, when the war commenced, when Jablanica was under blockade, and when it was shelled, I was assigned a task, the task of taking over the municipality building and the headquarters building which was empty. We phoned our colleagues who were a hundred metres away from us. They were our colleagues, our friends. They weren't aliens. We phoned them and told them to surrender and they did that. There was Marinko Ljoljo and there was another Marinko whose surname I can't remember. I sat down with them normally. I didn't interrogate them. I asked them about what was happening. If they are POWs, then they have to be handed over to the military police. Were they maltreated or taken away somewhere, I don't know about that. It's the military police battalion of the 6th Corps, or rather, at the time that was the 4th Corps that had its own unit in Jablanica. And they were under their authority. If they were maltreated, if crimes were committed against them, those who did these things should be held to account. I didn't imprison those individuals, I handed them over to the military police which is the normal procedure. I didn't have any prisons and I didn't have the authority to guard prisoners. Colleagues of mine from the brigade went to fortified positions. MUP representatives searched Croatian houses, and if I remember things correctly, they found 48 weapons there. That was on the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have understood your arguments. You handed these prisoners over to the military police, and you believe as of that point in time you were no longer responsible for them. Mr. Karnavas, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Obviously someone thought you were a responsible authority, otherwise they would not have brought the individual to you to question initially; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one handed them over to me. We contacted the people, we phoned, them and they came. We were a hundred metres away. Mr. Petkovic was in the HVO command. There was only a road dividing us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Very well. I want to go back to a document that was shown to you by the Prosecution, 2487. That was the document where I believe Ms. Alaburic wanted the Prosecution to look into a couple of paragraphs. And on the very -- on the second paragraph starting with: "On the 17th November 1992," it would appear from here that it describes the discussions that you talked about between the SDA and the HDZ with respect to allowing -- or Jablanica, the government, to be run or to be with or part of HZ HB. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's -- this is pretty accurate, is it not? We'll go step by step.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And -- now, in this paragraph they also talk about the use of the media to portray Croats in a certain manner or what their intentions were. Do you see that part, where it says: "The Jablanica SDA never responded to the invitation and used it to accuse us through the media, saying that we Croats" -- you see that, right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, that was occurring, was it not? There was a local TV station, was there not, in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that local TV station was used for propaganda purposes, was it not, sir? Yes, no, maybe, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know -- well, everything is propaganda in war. Media always uses propaganda. This --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This channel is trying to depict the events in town in an objective way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And this is the same media that you had appeared to give interviews, right? This is a CTV Jablanica, I believe that's what it was?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, did the Prosecution by any chance share with you a document that they provided with us and -- let me see if I can get the number here real quickly. It's 1D 01047.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if you could look to page 5, that's the portion that I'm going to be referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, sir, for your purposes if we could go -- there's a page that's circled number 75 or it would be page 6 in the B/C/S version. And here I have a document, sir. This is a statement from Mirko Zelenika, and you told us -- it would be page 3 for you. So it's page number 6 but it's page 3 for you in the B/C/S version. It starts with page 3 and you see where it says "press," you can see it. One, two, three, sort of the fourth paragraph. And this document here it says that this CTV Jablanica, namely the press service of the 44th Brigade, was the main source of information. And it goes on to say that it was characterising the HVO as pro-Ustasha, pro-fascist Croat force whose intent was to erase all traces of Muslims and Croats who were characterised as Ustasha. Now, that's the same radio station that we're talking about, the one that you said used propaganda, and the one that you had given interviews on; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that at all. I said that more or less all forms of media in wartime - I didn't provide any percentages, et cetera - all forms of media acted in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The press service of the 44th Brigade had its own programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That channel is still in existence today. Naturally, the brigade doesn't exist, but it had a 10- or 20-minute programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And people in Jablanica watched it, right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And of course, if this programme, the 44th Brigade is characterising the HVO as pro-fascist Ustashas, that's something that might cause some concern, would it not, both to the Muslim population and to the Croat population of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And you did not -- you're not denying that in fact that TV station, that television station that was locally broadcasting to the people in Jablanica was used for those purposes and that they were indeed characterising the Croats in that fashion? You're not denying --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I said literally. Likewise, I also didn't say that that term was never used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not denying the fact that that term was used. I'm not saying that no one used the term. We know who used such a term, but I didn't say much on this programme. Perhaps on one occasion, perhaps twice, I can't remember, but I don't think they were really in my favour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. But you would agree with us during that period of time relations between Croat and Muslim was rather fragile, tenuous, and that those sorts of comments on television by the Army of BiH was not - how should I put it? - conducive for peace, was it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I am concerned, I have already said that whenever I had contact with HVO commanders I attempted --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- to keep everything under effective control until the time at which Marko Zelenika was replaced. But the press service of the 44th Mountain Brigade was actually operational as at the time the conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Precisely. And that's what I'm saying. And I just want to make sure that we understand. I'm not accusing you of using those terms, but the Army of BiH, the 44th, was indeed using this propaganda tool to whip up the fears among the Muslims and to demonise the Croats; that's what I'm saying. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've had the opportunity of reading Mr. Petkovic's order. He calls the Muslims --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the greens in that order. It's the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. So I take it you don't want to answer the question?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, repeat it then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That tool was used for propaganda purposes in order to whip up the fears among the Muslims and demonise the Croats, was it not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The media didn't have that intention, but I won't say that that didn't happen on occasion but that wasn't their primary intention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. We'll leave it up to the Trial Chamber. Now, I want to go into less confrontational issues. We'll start off with the election. Now, according to the Prosecution indictment, they indicate that the population in Jablanica would have been approximately 18 per cent, while the population -- the Muslim population would have been approximately 71 per cent. Is that correct, more or less?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, there was a document shown to a previous witness with the pseudonym of BM who testified on the 20th and the 21st of September, wherein he was shown a book, a book that was referenced by an expert from the Prosecution in his so-called expert report or analysis, and this was -- the gentleman's name is Suad Arnautovic. And I'm referring to 1D 00920, and page 14 E, and on the B/C/S version it would be page 13. So page 14 for the English, page 14 -- page 14 English, page 13 B/C/S, just very briefly. The gentleman apparently went through the statistics and was able to provide us with a break-down. And I just want to focus on Jablanica. It's sort of in the middle, or the first -- top third. And it would appear that there were a total of 35 seats to be -- in Jablanica. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it says here of the 35, HDZ had gained seven seats; SDA had gained 15, then you have the Socialist Democratic Party with six; you have the Union of Yugoslav Reform Forces of BH, they had two; you had the Democratic Union with two; and then you had the -- your party, the SDP, with three. Would that be correct? And SDS gained zero seats, that would be the Serb party. Would that be correct? If you don't remember, just tell us you don't remember.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the party name isn't quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well -- but I'm more interested in the percentages with respect to HDZ and SDA.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They received an absolute majority and they formed a government.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now. Okay --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HDZ and the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, that's what I want to get to, because it would appear that if this chart is correct - and we have no reason to believe it's not - with 15 seats out of 35, SDA would have won 42.8 per cent, and HDZ would have won 20 per cent. Now --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that this information is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out of 35 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So this is -- I just want to -- let me conduct my cross. You said "absolute majority." The SDA did not have absolute majority in order to --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I said the SDA and the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In other words, HDZ was a coalition partner of SDA?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And like in any parliamentary system, a party can join a coalition and at some point can leave the coalition, right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. That's the point I just wanted to make and we'll move on to the next part. I want to show you some documents with respect to the Presidency. They don't require a great deal of commenting, just I want to make sure that we get this right. 1D 00779, if I could show you this, sir. This is a decision. It's on 9 April 1992, and I just want to focus our attention first of all at the preambular, because I think this is rather important with respect to the -- this alleged joint criminal enterprise issue that we're dealing with in this case. The preambular seems to indicate that the municipality of Jablanica has certain legislation, and this decision is based on this legislation. I'm talking about the statute.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And having lived in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time, it would be fair to say that every municipality had its own statute; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should have done. I can't say whether it did or did not, but it ought to have. How can it carry on life without an act of some kind?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactly. And it had its Official Gazette as well in order to publicise whatever decisions, decrees and what have you, right, so the people could be informed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, along with all of this --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Because we don't have time, Mr. President, I just wish to show very quickly to the gentleman several other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll first show you the documents, all of them, and then you can just -- I'll just ask you one big question or rather small question. 1D 00778, if we could pull that up. We see that this is a decision to establish a Presidency of Jablanica. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah. And if we go to the next page we see that the president was Sefer Hamdo; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And we'll be able to read this on our own. Next document is 1D 00340. This is a decision on the formation of Presidency. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see just the last part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. 1D 00340, I just want to make sure that what I'm showing you purports to be authentic documents which would be part of --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They should be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then the last document, 1D 00339. This is a decision on the appointment of members of the Presidency of Jablanica. Here we might want to rest a little bit, maybe take in the names.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do these names look familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except this is a different period of time. This is November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand that, sir, but we're going step by step. Okay? I just -- like Mr. Scott said, you know, Rome wasn't built in one day. So he was actually quoting Judge Liu. But anyway -- all right. So here are the names, and we see that it's sort of a multi-party, multi-ethnic Presidency; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, okay. That's all for that. Now if we could go on to the next chapter, and this would be the Crisis Staff. And before we get to the documents, first let me ask a couple of questions. At some point you called it a War Presidency, but what we're actually talking about is the Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sometimes they would call it that way. Sometimes they call it the Crisis Staff, the Presidency, they'd alternate, but they didn't exist in parallel terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And essentially the Crisis Staff was put in place in order to deal with the immediacy of the situation given that you had conflicts going on and it would have been too cumbersome to draft and to adopt legislation through normal channels; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that was the purpose of setting those bodies up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And just like on the last few documents, I'm going to go through the same process. First I want to show you 1D 00967. And again, if we could just look at the -- this is dated 5 May 1992. And it says at the preambular that again that this is pursuant to item 2 on a decision on the establishment of the Presidency of Jablanica. So it would seem to me that this decision is again grounded in legislation of the municipality of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And this was proper, was it not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it should have been, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, there's a reason why I'm going to be asking all of this. All right. Then we go on to another document, 1D 00777. This is a decision on the Crisis Staff organisational structure. Again, if we look at it. And if we go to the second page it seems that it's been signed by President Hamdo, Sefer. Do you see that, sir? This --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, again, he was -- he held that position, did he not, at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was the president of the municipality and president of that, but I can't see the whole document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, we -- we're not -- I'm not analysing the document, I just wanted to just --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah. And then, to make sure -- okay. Super. Then the next document I want to show you is 1D 00789, and these -- this is titled "rules of procedure." Again, this is for the benefit of the Trial Chamber so they can pour over these as we refer to them in our final briefs and arguments, as we make our case. But if you look at this, sir, it would be correct, would it not, that this was put in place at that point in time, 28 May 1992. It lays out how the Crisis Staff should operate.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Then I want to show you a document, 1D 00785. Okay. And I need to have this on the ELMO. I have to apologise. For some reason, this wasn't in the system. Okay. And in this decision, this is dated 11 May 1992. Again, if we see the preambular it shows that it's grounded in legislation from the municipality of Jablanica, and this is a decision to elect Mirko Zelenika of Jablanica, chairman of the Executive Committee of Jablanica municipality, and again it's signed by Hamdo Sefer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, if your memory serves you correctly, that is in fact the position that he held in that period of time, right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko Zelenika, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mirko, not Marko, Mirko.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe he replaced Palic, the man we mentioned yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, maybe, but I have a decision here that's signed by Hamdo Sefer that on 11 May 1992 he was appointed in that position.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Super, super. Okay. Now, we go to the next one, 1D 00787, and this is a decision. It's dated 14 May 1992. To elect the chairman, deputy chairman, members, and secretary of the Executive Committee of Jablanica. If you could look at that. Tell me if you look -- and look at the names and tell me if your memory serves you correctly whether indeed these members served in that capacity at that period in time.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they probably did. I don't see why they would not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And here we have a Marinko Zelenika. Is there any relations between Marinko, Marko, and Mirko?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you want to tell us, at least out of curiosity. I'm dying to know.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marko and Mirko is brothers, and Marinko I don't think belong to the same family. I can't claim that exactly. But there are a lot of Zelenikas anyway, a lot of that surname down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And the last decision, the last document I want to show you is 1D 001018. This is of 19 June 1992. It's a decision on the appointment of the members of the Jablanica Municipal Assembly Crisis Staff. Please look at it. Would this be correct, sir, and here we see that it's been signed by President Nijaz Ivkovic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a time when Hamdo Sefer was replaced, allegedly because of some sort of crime, and then a new man came. But that's not important now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But the important thing that I'm interested in is that -- here is a decision, 19 June 1992, where there is the appointment of the Jablanica Municipal Assembly Crisis Staff. And if we look at this, we see that you have Muslims and Croats on this Crisis Staff, correct, including Mirko Zelenika?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And that closes that chapter. Now, on the issue -- we're going to talk about another issue, and that is with respect to currency, the money that was circulating at the time. It's something that we need to sort of -- we need some assistance here. When you gave your first statement, sir, you had indicated that as of 1993 only the kuna was circulating, in your first statement. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1993, you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the kuna existed in 1992 as well -- well, not kuna but it was a Croatian coin. We used the German mark, and I don't know whether the kuna was used in 1992. It was a Croatian coin anyway and legal tender, but I'm not sure what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Step by step, sir. My questions are rather precise. In your first statement, in your first statement, you say, and I'm quoting now, "from January 1993 the only currency in use in Herzegovina was the Croatian kuna." Do you recall reading that in your first statement?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, what does Herzegovina mean there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, sir, sir, please, I'm just quoting you. You know what "Herzegovina" means; I don't. But this is what you said in your statement. It was provided to us by the OTP. You spent the day, maybe two days, with Mr. Scott going over your statements. Do you recall saying that? If you don't recall, that's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the part of Herzegovina controlled by the HVO, yes; now, the part of Herzegovina controlled by the BH army, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, very well --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But right up until the conflict -- up until the conflict, while we were able to travel to Croatia, of course we used Croatian currency, but not exclusively so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, I don't want to get bogged down on this. Trust me, if we had a couple of days we would go through this in great detail. But I have a statement here -- I have a statement here that you gave the first time to the OTP dated 10 May 2000; and then you were questioned again on 13th and 14th of June, 2000; and 5th and 12th of July, 2000. And I have this statement. And on page 20 of the statement with the ERN number on top of it is 01009507 it says in the second paragraph that you told the investigator: "From January 1993, the only currency in use in Herzegovina was the Croatian kuna." Do you recall, do you recall telling the investigators of OTP that? It calls for a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the part controlled by the HVO, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. And then later on when -- you gave another statement, did you not? You gave a second statement, and this would have been on 27 and 28 of June, 2002. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in that statement you corrected yourself or you said something differently. I would like to think that you corrected yourself, because, as I will demonstrate, it reflects the reality. If we look at the second-to-last paragraph on that -- on your statement on page 10 you say: "A lot of currencies were used all over Bosnia throughout end of 1992 and 1993. There was not an official currency at a state level." And then you go on to say: "In Sarajevo, the Bosnian dinar was used but in other parts of the country, Croatian kuna, Deutschemark, American dollar, and even some papers printed by commercial companies were used as currency. We were buying food and goods from Croatia and they would only take Croatian money or Deutschemarks. I think that there might have been an official decision on the use of the Croatian kuna as currency in Jablanica, and it was one of their currencies used as far as I remember, but I cannot confirm whether this decision was official or not." Do you recall making that statement?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. When I gave my first statement there were a lot of corrections to the statement because in the translation -- or I don't know how it came about, but the meaning of the statement was changed. So what is said there is true. I think it was an official decision whereby all the currencies were in use, the Croatian kuna, and the Deutschemark, and some of our internal pieces of paper and anything that allowed people to exchange goods and services for were used. There was no official currency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And that's what I'm going to go next into. If you just allow me to continue. If we could look at -- again, I'm going to go through a series of documents, and this is pertinent for other reasons. 1D 00976, if we could look at that, sir. This is dated in May 1992. It's unclear exactly -- I think it's 13 May 1992, and it says that this is a decision, "TO set up a team of experts who will put together a complete overview of the financial monetary flows in Jablanica municipality." Did you know Mr. Klepo?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And this is signed by Hamdo Sefer. Do you recall this decision or ...

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we weren't linked to the authorities over there; we did our job, they did theirs. But I do know that Mirsad Klepo was there working in the financial department and things like that, and he's in my company now engaged in finance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. So now we look at 1D 00786. This is dated 13 May 1992. This is an executive decision to form a working group for drafting documents necessary to overcome problems arising from dysfunctional system of payment, transactions, and fiscal and monetary policies in Jablanica municipality. Do you see this, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And do you recognise the list of names? There are six names in paragraph number 1, or Roman numeral I?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And looking at those names, being from a small town like Jablanica, could you tell us whether these are the kind of people, these individuals, that would have sort of the technical expertise to deal and tackle with this sort of an issue?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the list, were there any Muslims? Begovic, Ivkovic, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, there are, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Of the six, how many Muslims are there? By my count it looks like five.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five Muslims and one Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. All right. Now, moving right along, if we go to the next document, 1D 00984. This is a conclusion. And if we just look at it very quickly it says: "The Crisis Staff insists on the consistent implementation of an earlier order to ban the use -- order on the ban to use cash in the municipality without an order of the Jablanica Municipal Crisis Staff." And then it talks about the SDK, which is the payment bureau, the auditing service. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, at this period of time, 17 May 1992, the central bank of Bosnia isn't functioning, is it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether it was functioning in Sarajevo or not, but where we were down there it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And it seems to me -- I mean, if I look at all these documents, that the folks in the municipality in Jablanica were trying to -- trying to figure out how to best cope with the situation because money was needed; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah, and in fact the central SDK, the auditing service, wasn't working either, right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I know it's a little technical for many of us, it may be beyond the need at this point in time, but that was a rather important institution, was it not, back then, the SDK? I mean, I'm talking about before the war and even during the war, right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until the war, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the war, yes; not during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. During the war it wasn't functioning, right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And we'll have somebody who's a specialist talk about that. Now if we could go to -- to another decision -- to another -- yeah, decision, 1D 00991. This is dated 28 May 1992, and here it says - and this is just for illustrative purposes, by the way - under Roman numeral I it talks about a payment of 1 billion, is it, I guess 1.500.000 dinars for paying part of the salary to members of the TO --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I think it's 1 million 500.000.00 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You're very welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm starting to see things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this was on the 28th of May. Now, if we go to 29 May 1992, and here I think I'm going to go over this a little bit more carefully. Here, this says under Roman numeral I: "I hereby approve the use of 6.000 German marks of the collected voluntary contribution," and so on and so forth. So here we have a document where we have German marks being used as a currency, correct, and it's signed by the president. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You can't see it. Okay. This is 1D 00993. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll skip over that. We'll go over to the next one because I just -- that was just for illustrative purposes, but let's look at the one that I'm really interested in, 1D 00994. This is a decision, dated again, the same date, 29th --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now we're on to another document hopefully, 1D 00994, dated 29 May 1992. It's a decision, and I'm going to go -- I'm going to read, actually, Roman numeral I rather slowly because I think it is important. "In addition to the currency used, Yugoslav dinar, the German mark, DEM, and Croatian dinar, CRD, are hereby introduced as a means of payment into Jablanica municipality." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And this is a decision. And by this decision would it be correct to say that the Croatian dinar in the municipality of Jablanica is introduced by the municipality of Jablanica as an official currency during that period of time, as one of the official currencies?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. All right. And one last document, again for illustrative purposes so we don't lose the point, 1D 01017. If we could look at this. This is dated 17 June 1992. We have a -- this is a conclusion, and I just wish to point out that it talks about superpetrol and petrol, and we can see here in this official document that obviously was published in the Official Gazette of the Jablanica municipality that yes, indeed, the Croatian dinar is being used as a form of currency. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. That's all for that chapter. And I'm sure the Trial Chamber fully understands the purpose of this exercise. I want to get on to another topic, again something light. Taxes, the issue of taxes. Again, this is for other purposes, but I want to go to 1D 00320. And while that's being pulled up, let me ask you a few questions. During that period of time, the municipality of Jablanica found itself more or less like every other municipality in Bosnia-Herzegovina, where they needed funds in order to pay for the day-to-day affairs of the municipality. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it seems to me, if I heard you correctly, that by this point in time you could not, you could not, count on Sarajevo to provide the normal and vital financial services that one would expect in peacetime; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as finances were concerned, yes. The financial services were interrupted all over the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the -- under the control of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. But life went on in the municipalities, and of course every municipality, including Jablanica, had to find ways and means to meet their daily needs; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the documents we have had a look at just now show that people were trying to survive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Exactly. That's -- that's exactly the point I've been trying to make for months now. Now, if we go to this document, 1D 00320, we see that this is a decision on special war tax on personal income. We don't need to go through it. I just wish to point this out and to get this into evidence. We can dwell on this at some other point. But this to you, sir, would this not appear to be a valid piece of legislation that found itself in the Jablanica Official Gazette so everybody would know what their -- special tax, war tax, obligations were?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we feast our eyes a little bit, just a little bit, on the preamble, it seems -- we see that at the very beginning it starts off with the Law on All People's Defence, Article 73. Again, I want to point this out for the Trial Chamber because that's something that we've talked about in the past, because it seems to me - and correct me if I'm wrong - that at this period of time the Law on All People's Defence was particularly significant at the local level, was it not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this decision mainly concerns the decree law on financing social needs. It was issued by the government or the Presidency; I'm not quite sure by whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're talking about in the time of war, Article 73, Law on All People's Defence, and the point I'm trying to make is that if we want to begin to understand on what basis the municipalities were implementing various decisions, one must look at, among other things, the Law on All People's Defence. Would that be correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. If we go to the next document, this is 1D 00961. This is dated 28 December 1992. It's a decision on the formation of a tax police of Jablanica municipality. Nothing unusual of having a tax police, right, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This isn't really a field I feel at home with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the financial --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's not much I could say about finance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, financial police existed before, and this was a decision appointing three individuals to -- to form part of the tax police; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah. And just so we don't lose the point, all three are Muslims, are they not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm not saying anything one way or the other, but I'm just pointing that out. Now, if we look at one more document, 1D 01001 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, the last document under item 4 there is a representative of the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Did you designate someone as a member of this commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, and I don't remember that this police ever did anything. It wasn't possible to collect tax from anyone. At the time everyone was collecting tax, Mr. President. Each and every check-point collected tax. Banditry was omnipresent at the time, so there was nothing left to collect. There was banditry on all sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactly. That's my point. But when it does make reference to representative of BH -- of the armed forces, we're talking about -- we're not talking about HVO here, are we?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to go back to this time-period. This is December, the end of 1992. At the time, HVO representatives had already established their own government and had left the other body at the same time or there was a parallel Croatian power structure in existence in the municipality. There weren't any Muslims over there, there weren't any Croats over here, so it was a period during which there were these two parallel power structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it would seem to me that the Muslims were collecting taxes for themselves, their own people, and the Croats were doing the same for their people, at least in Jablanica, if I'm understanding you correctly with these two parallel structures?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it was everywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. I'm somewhat perplexed by your answer. You have mentioned two parallel governments. I was following the demonstration the Defence is trying to make very carefully, and my question is: In the Presidency of this municipality, were there Croats as well as Muslims at the time to -- at the same time, or were there Muslims and Croats here and then there was another structure that only consisted of HVO Croats. Can you clarify that for me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You should bear in mind the chronology up until November and the beginning of December. There was a single body. You have already seen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're saying up until the beginning of December everything was unified?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, up until the end of 1992 everything was more or less integrated. There was just one single body. It wasn't ideal, but it functioned somehow. But after that point in time, we've seen from other documents that there were two power structures in place. When I attended those meetings on the seizing power -- well, I said: Okay, let's establish two power structures. Anything's better than fighting. If you think it's better to have two power structures, fine, but let's just have peace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're going to get to that, and we're going to see how things develop. But just one last document on the issue of taxes. 1D 01001. This seems to be a conclusion by the president of the Jablanica Municipal Assembly Presidency I guess, and it says here - and this is, by the way, dated 6 January 1993 - where they're imposing an obligation of 300 Deutschemarks, German marks, for armed forces on the production of valid and promptly issued written proof, and that's for citizens that are temporarily living outside, living abroad and working in Croatian enterprises; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Just a very small point. In my document it says "7 January."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In B/C/S it says "7" and in the -- you're right. You're right. I guess I was looking at -- at the session held on 6th January. I stand corrected. It's dated 7 January from a session the day before where they -- there's this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall this, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At all levels people were trying to get money, so a conclusion or a decision would be taken according to which people working abroad and whose families were living in Bosnia should spend -- should pay 300 marks a month. But who's going to implement that decision? Who's going to force someone who works in Germany to pay 300 marks? These decisions had no force; they couldn't be implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, all I'm saying -- all I'm trying to demonstrate here is that what the Prosecution accuses the Croats of doing, we see that the Muslims are doing the same in this municipality and other municipalities. We're going to see that; that's the point I'm trying to make. Now, if we could go --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, there are two matters here. Mr. Karnavas, you have another three minutes left --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Three minutes. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just waiting. I didn't want to interrupt Mr. Karnavas and I've tried very hard not to, but during -- at this point, based on what he just said, I just want to make it very clear, it's never been the proposition of the Prosecution with this witness, and in fact quite the contrary, that throughout most of 1992, despite the fact that this was a heavily Muslim majority municipality, that the institutions remained multi-ethnic, multi-party until very late that year, and we never pretended or suggested anything to the contrary. And in fact it's to the credit of the Muslims in Jablanica that it remained that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to get into a debate. I know I started at 12.00, I believe, I have an hour and there were some questions from the Bench which shouldn't be deducted from me. And I think we're moving along at a rather -- very fast pace, if I might say so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but when I said that you had another three minutes, well, that excluded the Judges' time. So the Judges' questions were deducted. These are the calculations that the registrar has provided me with. But -- because the registrar can calculate the seconds used by having recourse to this electronic system. I've just used five seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. Well, just for the record, because I want to make sure that this is heard loud and clear throughout the world that I spent an enormous amount of time putting together what I believe is a very lean cross-examination and to protect my client and all the other clients against the joint criminal enterprise. And this is precisely the type of measure being imposed on us that directly impact on my client's human rights, and the human rights not in a conceptual matter in some classroom, not in the abstract, but in a courtroom, so I will try to do my best, but at some point I will need to make my record to get all my documents in. Because I think this is unfair to put such stringent limitations on us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, let's go through -- just a couple of quick questions here on blocking of roads. Sir, I want to show you -- I want to show you 1D 00958.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And this is precisely, Your Honour, why I have to be rude with the witnesses and cut them off which I find terrible because they come and want to give their full evidence, and I'm forced to be rude in order to make up time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you believe that the question is very important, your colleagues can give you some of their time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But I'm trying -- I have to ask them to represent their clients -- you know, that's not the point. The point is they shouldn't be placed in a position where they're bartering their time, Your Honour. I understand. I'm trying to be efficient. 1D 00958. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could look at the decision on approving the blocking of roads. This is 25 April 1992, and if we look at Article 1, and it's important, sir, if you could help us out here because there seems to be - at least I'm told - that perhaps one of the words is not translated correctly. So if you could read Article 1 for us so we can get a translation.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I read it out?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We hereby authorise the Jablanica TO staff to place obstacles on the road from Jablanica to Mostar, depending on how the situation develops and on the basis of their own professional assessment."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I'm told by my colleague here that again the interpretation may not be quite as accurate, and I'm referring to the word "zarusavanje," if I could ask the witness what is his understanding of that word?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The word "zarusavanje" means bringing in material, placing it on the road so that it can't be used. You can either blow up an area just above the road so that the debris falls on the road and makes it impossible to use the road. That's what would be meant by the term "zarusavanje."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you, I thought that was an important point to point out at this point in time. I'm going to try to skip most of it and at some point I'll make my record. I want to show you a document, 1D 00963. This is a decision. It's on 1 May 1992. I just want to point out something that might be interesting and goes to the -- some of our previous testimony as to why the Croats might have had some misgivings with respect to some of the internationals or their alleged allies. Here it says: "Decision" -- we see here in this decision 1 May 1992 to give 2.500 meals, given as aid by the UN High Commissioner to the Jablanica Territorial Defence. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This was humanitarian aid that was not intended for the -- for the Territorial Defence, was it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. At this time we already held positions facing the Serbs, and all we could give people is the humanitarian aid to take up with them because they'd spend up to a week up there --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The high commissioner was giving you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, you have to stop now because unfortunately we won't have sufficient time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have time from the Stojic Defence team and at some point, as I said, I wish to make my record as far as the documents, if for no other reason, for the Appeals Chamber such as -- and I believe I also -- I'm also being given ten from Mr. Praljak's Defence team. I appreciate the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, when you refer to an appeal, you are threatening the Judges --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and this is unacceptable. If you want to make an appeal, you will do so, but don't repeat this every time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I note that the Stojic Defence has granted you ten minutes. Make good use of those ten minutes rather than speak about an appeal you might lodge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm making my record, Your Honour. That's what the whole point of making my record, and that's why when you indicated that time would be subtracted from the Defence for trying to make a record through -- through objections, that was the whole purpose. It's the purpose to make a record for appeal purposes. And without a record, I'm not being due diligent. Without a record, I cannot appeal. Without getting these documents in the record, and I don't know how I can get a document in record without a witness. I just can't read documents. Otherwise both sides should bring in a truck-load each with their own documents and say, here, Your Honours, read it, and we'll write final briefs on it. This is not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
