utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the documents that are not familiar with you can show them to this witness. Your colleagues can also do this. There will be other witnesses. You'll be calling your own witnesses. Don't say that you cannot present your own documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that I can bring it through another witness. You're saying I have a burden to bear. What makes you think that I don't want to put on a case? Maybe the Prosecution will not put on their case. But when you say bring it through my case, the burden is being shifted. That's the whole point. And why not -- why not bring fewer witnesses on the Defence when I have a good witness right here and I can bring all these documents in. That's all I'm trying to do. I'm just trying to do my job. I'm just trying to be a good lawyer. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour. I mean, just appropriate to this dialogue just now, I mean, unfortunately many of these points that have been put to the witness are not disputed. The Prosecution's never disputed that these were multi-ethnic, multi-party authorities for most of 1992. So that hasn't been in dispute. It's also -- I just find it interesting, these last two exhibits that Mr. Karnavas has put to the witness about the money to the TO and the obstructions on the road, these are decisions that were made by exactly the same multi-ethnic, multi-party bodies, including Croats, that he's just spent the last 45 minutes proving to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, yesterday as of April 1992 the Prosecution was alleging that the joint criminal enterprise was already in place. They planted the seed. That's why I had to go through this, because he was the one that brought it up. They were trying to get this gentleman to say that as of April 1992 there was a joint criminal enterprise and they began destroying roads and destroying the tunnels, and that's what I'm trying to show at this point in time. At this point you have joint defences. The situation on the ground is extremely and highly complex. It's not black and white, as Mr. Scott would have us to believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sorry, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I didn't see a decision by the joint bodies in -- that should be 1992 approving the destruction of the Aleksin Han bridge. It's a completely different situation and, I'm sorry, but Mr. Karnavas is comparing apples and oranges. These are decisions made by the joint Croat-Muslim bodies, and I didn't see a document yesterday that talks anything about destroying the Aleksin Han bridge for one example.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The decision I demonstrate, I showed was a policy. It was not bridge by bridge, tunnel by tunnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me go on to the next portion. And let me skip ahead a little bit. The Prosecution has not mentioned an individual by the name of Cibo. Do you know who this person is?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And at one point in time he was appointed to be in charge of the municipalities of - what was it? - Jablanica, Prozor, and Konjic. Did I get it right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And he was appointed by Izetbegovic, right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall about what time?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mid-March, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And in fact when Cibo came, and as I understand it he's either under investigation or in litigation being charged with crimes of his own during this period of time at the local courts, when he came, the situation got rather worse on the ground, did it not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we're moving into another area now. It was March 1993 at the time, and the situation on the ground was fairly difficult. There were two --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, sir, sir --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- governments in existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just want to know when he came, because we're going to go step by step. He came about that time --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, help me out here, sir. On what legal authority did Izetbegovic appoint Cibo to be the president of three municipalities? I'm sure you must have pointed it out to Mr. Scott and his team to show on what grounds Mr. Cibo was appointed the head of three municipalities at this point in time. What was the law?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when war broke out, they issued decree laws to regulate daily life --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, sir, sir --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- we didn't have those rules --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We just went through all that process of showing legislation at the municipality. That was the purpose of that exercise that took up so much time, so we could all see that in Jablanica there is a process. I'm asking you: Do you know concretely - yes, no, maybe, I don't know - on what legal authority did Izetbegovic appoint this man to be in charge of three municipalities, even though we had elections back in 1991, and that's where we started? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know on the basis of which rules this was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Thank you, sir. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But let me assist you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you don't want me to, that's fine --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we can look at 1D 00949, and this is from Konjic. We don't have anything from Jablanica, but this is something that I have in Konjic and I'm going to go through the middle of the page. This is a conclusion, 29 March 1993, and it's with respect to Dr. Cibo. And in the middle of the page, it says, and I'll read it in English: "There is no explanation for the decision of the Presidency RBiH so that we do not know what the reasoning was for the eminent body's decision," that was the decision to appoint this gentleman. You, sir, were in Jablanica at the time. Were you provided with an explanation by Izetbegovic or the SDA or anybody else as to how and on what basis Cibo was appointed?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he arrived in Jablanica he gathered us. He showed us three documents. That's what I wanted to say. It wasn't just a document showing that he was a member of the municipality, but he was also a member of the corps command and he was the main person in the SDA. He was given absolute authority. We didn't agree with this; we wanted to reject this. But at the same time that he came, certain other military formations arrived down there. So we didn't want to implement the decision, but we were afraid of an internal conflict. So we accepted him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah, but my whole -- sir --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no, but the point I'm trying make is this, the point I'm trying to make is this: That you have Izetbegovic doing whatever he wants, because I'm asking you concretely on what basis can this person appoint someone for three municipalities when you had local elections, when you had a process, when the municipalities were forming, you know, whether it's a Crisis Staff or a War Presidency, whatever you want to call it, where they're making decisions, where they're adopting currencies? On what basis did Izetbegovic decide that, from this point on, somebody from the outside, not elected, was going to be on top of everybody, including the Croats, in Jablanica, Konjic, and Prozor?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's clear. The question is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll answer the question. I'm not familiar with the rule. I don't know whether it existed or not, but I'm not familiar with such rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: His presence caused a great deal of discontent, did it not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, amongst us, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when the Croats, at one point you said -- you had indicated in your testimony that at some point, and I believe it was in December or November of 1992, that they had made a request that perhaps Jablanica municipality should join in with the HZ HB; correct? Do you remember that conversation when we first started?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And there was no agreement; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so the Croats decided to leave the government, right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The HDZ, right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Which had been elected and they were a coalition party, and under the rules and regulations, they were clearly entitled to just leave the coalition; it is being done all over Europe today. They could elect, right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And at the time, if I understand you correctly, when there was a so-called ultimatum in January, you said nobody took it seriously because there were only about 400 Croats and 2.500 Muslim fighters over there, right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So clearly if there was a conflict -- 300 Croats. If there was a conflict, we could say clearly, at least numerically speaking, the Muslims had the upper hand; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- on the territory of the municipality, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And if I look at your statement, you indicated that there was some kind of an ultimatum of such that was initially -- that was initially given by Bozo Rajic in December, in December, 1992. That's not correct, is it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Exactly -- well, you said -- you gave two dates. You said there were two occasions. But there was no ultimatum, just to be on the safe side, just to be clear --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was sometime in mid-January 1993 that that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And today you were asked by the Prosecutor who was Bozo Rajic, and you indicated that he was the Minister of Defence for Herceg-Bosna; correct? That was your understanding.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably said that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And it's -- in fact, it's stated in your document, in your statement, because I have proofing notes from the Prosecutor dated 5 November 2006 wherein, under point number 6, apparently you pointed out or you made a correction where you indicate that Bozo Rajic was actually the Minister of Defence for the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. There's no dilemma on that; that's the position he held, so you were mistaken --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right, yes. All right. I got it mixed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I've been given some additional time, Mr. President, thanks to my colleagues, and I hope I don't abuse it because they have things that they need to do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which colleagues?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which ones?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have -- I had ten minutes from Mr. Praljak, I had ten minutes from Mr. Coric, and I believe I already got ten minutes from Mr. Stojic. And if I could have an accounting, that way I can -- I'm moving as fast as I can, Mr. President, and this is a Herculean task and I'm only 5 foot 8. Can I proceed, Mr. President? I was waiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have 73 minutes -- used up 73 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And I wish to apologise for my earlier outburst. I've just been up all night trying to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I can't change my personality now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could just talk a little bit about mobilisation, the issue of mobilisation. And if we can go to document 1D 00955. Again, this is dated 25 April 1992. We see that this is a -- this regards to work obligation; correct? All you got to do is look at the first paragraph under Roman numeral I: "All men and women from ages 18 to 60 years of age shall perform the work obligation service."

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we go -- and that would have been for both Croat and Muslim; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It ought to have been, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Another document, just very quickly, 28 April 1992, this is an order. Again, everybody is subject to -- 1D 00960. This deals with work obligation. Incidentally, when you were appointed -- because I was rather unclear. When they established the 44th Brigade and you were left behind in Jablanica, were you part of the ABiH or were you fulfilling the function of -- of civil protection?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remained a member of the armija.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you were not doing civil protection work?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Again, just very quickly, 1D 00974, we have -- this is an order dated 11 May 1992. And this talks about seizing and mobilising all materiels and technical equipment. Now, in light of the earliest piece that we received from the Prosecution it would seem to be that at this point in time, at this point in time, consistent with the situation on the ground, the municipality had the ability and in fact was indeed mobilising and seizing materiel as it sought fit; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the Ministry of Defence; it did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactly, exactly. And at that point in time, at least back in 11 May 1992, that would have included -- the HVO was still cooperating and working with, closely allied to the Army of BiH?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we look at 13 May 1992, there's another order there, and this is kind of interesting, again for other purposes. It talks about TO return the persons who fled other municipalities are staying in Jablanica -- oh, I'm sorry, 1D 00977. Here's an order dated 13 May 1992 to return the persons who fled other municipalities are staying in Jablanica municipality and are fit to serve in the army or work to the municipalities where -- whence they came and their refugee status be suspended. It seems to me that from this order able-bodied men from other municipalities had to go back to do their patriotic duty wherever they came from; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's partially it, but what this was about is this: In May 1992 we had a large number of refugees from Foca, and they had their own brigade which existed in the territory of Trnovo and Igman, up there. Now, these were really ludicrous situations. The men put on women's clothing. They had those Muslim women's pantaloons and things like that, and there were a large number of people hiding there. That was a great problem for us. We would collect up a whole bus of people like that and they were taken to Igman and then they would come back. So this order was linked to the problem of refugees, exclusively men from Foca who were not returned to Foca but it was the so-called 1st Foca Brigade which existed in the region of Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... refugees, just to make sure that we understand, you indicated that at some point Jablanica had up to 10.000 refugees. During the earlier part of the conflict when it was, you know, the Serbs were the aggressors, there were quite a few refugees that came into Jablanica, right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, most of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that the accommodations were rather scarce?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just say yes.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. All right.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was absolutely no possibility and that's why the council intervened with three camps down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. But also as I understand it, folks were -- you know, refugees were being put into residence where others were living in. In other words, if a family had a large residence, other refugees would come in to occupy part of the residence, to share it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were all kinds of situations. Most of them were put up in the schools, sports halls, and camps later on when they were erected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, did it occur where refugees were coming in to share folks' homes that lived in Jablanica? It's a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The staff for the accommodation of refugees was in charge of putting up the refugees. It was a special body set up by the municipality that was functioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, sir --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, wait for me to finish. Wait for me to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just want you to give me an answer.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry that you don't have the time, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I know. Complain about it. I'm asking you a very simple question. Were refugees forced or asked to reside in people's homes, to share their homes, by this commission?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there was that, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And that might have caused some tension, too, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the very presence of 10.000 people in a town which normally has a population of 3.000 would cause --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. We'll move on. We'll move on, sir. Let me show you another document, 1D 00986. And here it says -- this is an order dated 19 May 1992. The Jablanica public security station in here ordered the return, you know, hereby ordered to return to their place of residence all men fit to work who are currently staying in Jablanica municipality as refugees from the municipalities of Konjic and Mostar. So here this is an order basically asking folks to leave, right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these were people who had fled from obligations. We had a flood of people from Mostar and Konjic, Konjic was close by, who had fled from up there --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- not to have to go and join the army. And now, do you think that somebody should look after them, take care of them, of course they should be expelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That's what I wanted to hear. And this is a decision that -- this is an order that's signed by Hamdo Sefer, right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May he burn in ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm told that in the transcript it says apparently not -- your entire answer didn't -- wasn't recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The reason that they fled, was that because they didn't want to do their military service or their work obligation?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, just that. It didn't refer to the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Right --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's time. Your time is up, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very -- very well, Mr. President. I think that -- very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Several seconds. Mr. Karnavas, while you were asking questions, I listened to you and I consulted your dossier and I see that you have provided for 50 documents here. The exact number of 50. Now, if we take a minimum of one minute per document, that means that in advance you would have exceeded your 45 minutes. So you should have told us at the outset that your colleagues gave you such and such an amount of time because it's easy to provide for 50 documents, present 20, and then start shouting at the Chamber and saying that they prevented you from showing the other 30 documents. So if you prepare 50 documents in advance, you must know that you won't be able to get through all those documents unless other people give you their time and so on. So with these 50 documents I'm sure that there is one that is essential, others that perhaps are not. They're not all of equal value, and it's up to you to select the ones that you consider to be most important and present them. So that's food for thought for you. Try and find a better solution and save us from wasting time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I will -- I continue to fine-tune my skills, but I was rather ambitious. I thought I was able -- I was going to get through all the documents. I take your point, and I didn't mean to raise my voice to the Trial Chamber, though at times I feel I must be heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you will be coming back tomorrow. I don't know if we'll get through the cross-examination tomorrow. It depends on the Defence counsel. The counsel for General Petkovic have 35 minutes, the others 45 minutes or whatever, and perhaps they will see that Mr. Karnavas might have asked some of the questions that they were going to answer [as interpreted]. So I can't say whether your testimony will be finished tomorrow. As I said, don't speak to anybody between now and tomorrow, and we start the hearing tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 8th day of November, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
